one_liner: Experimental AVX-512 ChaCha20-Poly1305 assembly for x86-64 Linux; 19-48% fewer cycles/byte than OpenSSL's assembly on AMD Zen 5.
what_it_does: A small C library (one header, one C glue file, perlasm and NASM kernels) that provides raw ChaCha20 (one-shot CRYPTO_chacha_20 and a streaming CHACHA20_CTX) and RFC 8439 ChaCha20-Poly1305 seal/open with a 12-byte nonce, in contiguous-tag and scatter/gather (detached-tag) forms. The function shapes follow BoringSSL, not OpenSSL EVP, so call sites must be rewritten. CPUID dispatch at load time picks the fused AVX-512 AEAD; other CPUs fall back to OpenSSL-derived ChaCha kernels plus a portable C Poly1305. The author describes the project as an experiment in using idle execution ports, not a hardened product.
how_it_is_fast: It uses function stitching: raw ChaCha20 runs one extra block in scalar GPRs alongside 8 (AVX2, 9x) or 16 (AVX-512, 17x) vector blocks, and ChaCha20_32x interleaves two independent 16-block ZMM states to raise instruction-level parallelism from 4 to 8, reloading the initial state from broadcast memory operands so no registers are spilled. The AEAD is a BoringSSL/Cloudflare-style stitched loop ported to AVX-512: ChaCha on vector ports encrypts chunk i while two scalar mulx Poly1305 chains on the integer ports authenticate two contiguous 512-byte halves of chunk i-1, joined as A*r^32+B, with Intel IPsec-MB's staggered issue order. For 1025-2048-byte packets, 'key-mode' kernels (25x/33x) compute the counter-0 Poly1305 key block in scalar registers in the same call as the payload, which removes a second kernel launch the README puts at about 400 cycles. Tails larger than 768 bytes use an AVX-512 IFMA52 Poly1305 and a modular power ladder to merge the split accumulators.
when_to_use: Linux x86-64 servers on AMD Zen 5 or Zen 4 (AVX-512F/BW/VL, AVX-512 IFMA and BMI2 present) where ChaCha20-Poly1305 record encryption is a measurable share of CPU time.
WireGuard, QUIC and TLS-record-sized payloads (about 1.2-1.5 KB) on Zen 5: seal takes 0.94 c/B against 1.72 for OpenSSL's assembly and 2.00 for BoringSSL's stitched AVX2 at 1360-1420 B.
Bulk ChaCha20 keystream of 4 KB or more with AVX-512: 0.36 c/B against 0.54 for OpenSSL's 16x kernel at 32-64 KiB on Zen 5.
A custom data plane (userspace VPN, own QUIC stack) that can call a raw C AEAD function directly instead of going through EVP.
As reference code for port-level stitching, dual-state ILP and single-dispatch key generation, to port into a maintained crypto library.
when_not_to_use: CPUs without AVX-512 IFMA (every AVX2-only machine, Skylake-SP-family Xeons): the AEAD then runs OpenSSL-derived ChaCha plus a portable C radix-2^26 Poly1305, a path result.md does not benchmark and that has no assembly Poly1305.
Messages of 256 bytes or less: Zen 5 seal is 20-24% slower than OpenSSL's assembly at 64-256 B (Zen 4: 9.5-23% slower), and fixed per-call cost is 762 cycles against 650.
Raw AVX-512 ChaCha20 at 1200-1420 B: it loses to Intel IPsec-MB by 4-8% on Zen 5 and 17-26% on Zen 4; on Zen 4 the AEAD only ties Intel at 4-9 KB (-1.3% at jumbo frames).

Production or compliance-bound systems: single author, 3 commits, no releases, no audit, fuzzing or FIPS story, hand-written crypto assembly; Intel CPUs, AVX-512 frequency effects and SMT neighbours are untested.
Non-Linux or non-x86-64 targets (macOS, Windows, ARM), or protocols needing XChaCha20 or extra_in: the build emits ELF only, the nonce is 12 bytes, and seal_scatter rejects extra_in.

integration.dependencies: none at runtime; the build needs GNU make, gcc, Perl (perlasm), NASM and GNU ld; `make test` also links OpenSSL libcrypto to cross-check results; the benchmark harness dlopens Intel's libIPSec_MB
integration.min_toolchain: gcc with GNU as 2.25+ (the inherited perlasm emits the AVX-512 paths only when it detects GNU as >= 2.25); exact gcc and NASM versions not documented
integration.platforms: Linux x86-64 (ELF) only. The fast AEAD path needs AVX2, BMI2, AVX-512F/BW/VL and AVX-512 IFMA; benchmarked only on AMD Zen 4 and Zen 5; other x86-64 CPUs get the fallback
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. Seal/open keep no shared state beyond CPU-feature globals set by a load-time constructor; chacha20_poly1305_set_avx512_enabled() rewrites those globals without synchronisation, so do not call it while other threads encrypt. CHACHA20_CTX is per-caller state.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — BoringSSL-style C functions (CRYPTO_chacha_20, chacha20_poly1305_seal/open, seal_scatter/open_gather), not an OpenSSL EVP cipher, provider or BoringSSL EVP_AEAD; call sites must change

gotchas: Symbol clashes: the library exports CRYPTO_chacha_20 (a BoringSSL public name) and ChaCha20_ctr32, and defines OPENSSL_ia32cap_P unless built with -DCHACHA20_USE_OPENSSL_CAP. Static linking next to OpenSSL or BoringSSL can therefore fail; the repo's own Makefile renames the vendored OpenSSL symbols with -D flags for this reason.

The README example links build/chacha20poly1305.a, but the Makefile builds only build/aead512.o and build/chacha20poly1305.o (no archive target). The Makefile also warns that aead_mac_partial.o must stay before aead512_core.o in link order to avoid a Zen 5 MAC-drain alignment regression.
On the AVX-512 path, open decrypts into the output buffer before it compares the tag, and zeroes the buffer on failure. Check the return value before using the output.
Batch-boundary lengths (1024, 2048, 4096 B) flatter the kernels; the author says the 2048 B margin is about double the margin 200 B to either side. Benchmark at your real packet sizes.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick ChaChaCha only when ChaCha20-Poly1305 record encryption itself is the bottleneck on AVX-512 IFMA x86 servers and you can call a raw AEAD function, as in a custom WireGuard or QUIC data plane. For a complete, maintained TLS stack pick AWS-LC or wolfSSL; for AES-GCM traffic, picotls's fusion engine is the equivalent stitched-AEAD choice.
verified_claims_summary: The author measured core cycles per byte (perf_event_open, one pinned core, best of 7 repetitions x 3 runs, 13-byte AAD, hot-cache loop over one buffer with a fixed key, round-trip check before timing) on AMD EPYC 9655 (Zen 5) and EPYC 4244P (Zen 4), with gcc -O2 C glue around hand-written assembly. Baselines were OpenSSL's vendored chacha-x86_64/poly1305-x86_64 assembly (commit bee02b7d) called directly, BoringSSL's stitched AVX2 AEAD and Intel IPsec-MB 3.0.0-dev. On Zen 5, AEAD seal used 19-45% fewer cycles per byte than OpenSSL's assembly across 1.2 KB-64 KiB bands and 49-57% fewer than BoringSSL; on Zen 4 it used 9-33% fewer than OpenSSL and roughly tied Intel IPsec-MB (-1.3% to +8.9%).
status_note: Active but brand new: 3 commits between 2026-08-14 and 2026-09-21 by one author, 1 star, no releases or issues. Apache-2.0 with retained OpenSSL, BoringSSL/Cloudflare (ISC) and Intel (BSD-3) code, and small enough to vendor, but the crypto assembly is unaudited.
